note: ysim parameter table (generated by ysim/params.py); SI units
rule_S:
, the resolution of the unit problem of the authors' MJCF:
  The authors' MJCF is written in decimetres and grams with gravity 9.81 "dm/s^2" (= 0.981 m/s^2 in SI). Read
  literally in SI (k_SI = k_model * 1e-3 N/m) the robot collapses under real gravity and the published gait does
  not travel (measured: 32 mm in 537 s). The authors' model is self-consistent only as a 1/10-g world. To
  keep its static shapes (which is what its primitives and its sysID refer to) under 9.81 m/s^2 with the same
  masses and geometry, every force must scale by 10: spring stiffness x10; viscous damping x sqrt(10) (force x10,
  time x 1/sqrt(10)); direct contact solref stiffness [1/s^2] x10 and damping [1/s] x sqrt(10). Friction is
  dimensionless and unchanged. Motor speed is NOT scaled (the real motor runs at its vendor speed).
  ysim 0.3.0: Rule S stays for the elastic members (the stretch sensors, whose stiffness in the authors' file is a
  model of silicone strips), the tendon damping and the contact; it is NOT used for the fishing line, a material
  with a known construction (braided UHMWPE, 100 lb): the line's stiffness follows the material rule k = EA / L.

Basis: the mean re-planning delay (settle_after, 0.911 s) is longer than the rest phase lasts in this model (median 0.27 s, p90 0.59 s, max 1.30 s over 264 validation executions), so on the robot the rest phase normally completes before the plan arrives; the skip only happens when a plan comes back faster than the rest phase

execution_mode.rule: the default is the authors' own code (mode 'hardware') if with it every published forward roll reaches the next face from every face; it does not (0 / 108: from 035 / 125 / 134 a roll only switches to the pair partner, from 025 / 124 / 034 it stays; ysim 0.3.0 the same), so the default is mode 'tracked' (ASSUMPTION track_tol)

track_tol.source: the authors' control code stops a motor once |pos - target| < 0.15 (0.35 for ranges >= 130; $YSIM_SOURCES/gh_ChemStud24_tensegrity/repo branch rss25 @4b79620 src/run_tensegrity_Astar.py lines 56-57, 569-572); with that band no forward roll of this model reaches the next face (the band study, 0 / 108; ysim 0.3.0 and 0.2.0 found the same)
track_tol.rule: mode 'tracked' runs the same published target states, ranges, PID and motors to within this band of the range for every target, with the authors' simulator slack rule (params slack_rule), and ends with the rest phase at the same band. Value = the widest band of the ladder 15 / 10 / 7 / 5 % at which every published forward roll reaches the next face class (the class the authors' next_nodes predicts) in every execution from every rollable face (the faces the robot lives on: 07 starts on any of the six); chosen on that tipping criterion only, never on the table's distances; re-run on ysim 0.3.1 with the same rule: still 5 %
track_tol.sensitivity: the band study (0.3.1), rolls reaching the next face: 15 % 21/108 (only roll_140_140 12/12 and roll_120_140 9/12), 10 % 80/108 (the rolls with right range 100 fail), 7 % 100/108 (roll_100_100 4/12), 5 % 108/108; the authors' band (mode hardware) 0/108. ysim 0.3.0 with the 0.3.0 hook rule: 3 / 72 / 97 / 108. Where a roll tips its distance hardly depends on the band (mean 0.246 / 0.243 / 0.240 / 0.234 m at 5 / 7 / 10 / 15 %); duration per roll 7.2 / 6.9 / 6.4 / 5.7 s at 5 / 7 / 10 / 15 % (hardware 5.0 s, not tipping). Cost: the model needs a band three times tighter than the authors' code to roll every roll (the real robot rolls with 15 %), so it is harder to tip than the real robot; every state ends closer to its target and the rest shape is held at 200 +- 5 mm instead of the code's 200 +- 15 mm. Candidate causes (none tested to a conclusion): the free hook choice, the strongest (params hook_roles: across the 64 assignments the guide allows a uniform 15 % band tips 0-18 of 18 rolls, (4, 6) and (4, 7) all 18, and the authors' code verbatim tips up to 13 / 18; those assignments lie far from the authors' model, M 16.5-19.4 mm, so they are only reported), sensor lengths measured between the real hooks 10 mm off the axis, the full collision spheres 3 mm fatter than the end caps below their equator, all mass on the axis

hook_roles.value: S_out = the hook nearest the line guide; about the strut's +z axis (odd -> even node) the roles follow S_out, L, S_in, I at +90 deg steps at both ends (even ends: as ysim 0.3.0; odd ends: I and L exchanged against 0.3.0)
hook_roles.source: assembly guide tensegrity.yale.edu Guide_to_assembly_a_tensegrity_robot_V3.pdf (sha256 912c44cc...) PDF p26 (printed page 24): 'It does not matter which of the hooks on the end caps the fishing line is connected to'; PDF p27 (printed page 25): 'The long sensors must be connected to the opposite hook of the fishing line', 'The short sensors must be connected in parallel to the fishing lines' (no hook named). So every end allows 8 assignments (I on any of the 4 hooks, L opposite, the two short sensors on the other two in either order; geometry.allowed_end_assignments), 64 per strut: the role per hook is the builder's free choice, not derived. The authors' own simulation model ($YSIM_SOURCES/gdrive_crgs/extracted/crgs_3_bar_dataset/dataset_0/3bar_new_platform_all_cables.xml lines 107-224, copied in notes/sim_base_data/authors_model.json): at all six ends S_out, L, S_in, I follow at +90 deg steps about the strut's odd -> even axis and the line guide sits 13-27 deg from S_out on the I side; each end's cross is turned toward the partner nodes of their initial pose, so the two crosses of one strut differ by 132-140 deg, while the real strut's hooks sit at the same azimuths at both ends and its two ends are two-fold symmetric. ysim 0.3.0's rule (S_out nearest the guide, I its neighbour on the guide side) kept the guide relation but gave the mirror image of the authors' arrangement at the odd ends; it ranks 15th of 64 by the rule below
hook_roles.rule: the allowed assignment nearest the authors' simulation model by M = sqrt((M_strut^2 + M_end^2) / 2), where each mesh strut is placed on the authors' node axis of their initial pose and M_strut = RMS 3D distance of its 10 attachment sites (S_out, S_in, I, L, line guide; both ends) to the authors' sites of the same roles with one roll per strut (absolute geometry, both ends), M_end = the same with a roll per end (each end's arrangement in the strut frame; no mirror image allowed: a rigid strut cannot be mirrored); RMS over the 3 struts (geometry.assignment_distance). Chosen, assignment (6, 5): 10.68 mm. Runner-up (0, 5), 11.77 mm: the same cyclic order at both ends, but at the even ends I instead of S_out on the hook nearest the guide. 0.3.0's rule (6, 1): 15.60 mm, 12 assignments nearer, tied with 3 others for places 13-16. Each part alone is nearly tied between two candidates (M_strut: (0, 5) 11.78 vs (6, 5) 11.83 mm; M_end: (6, 6) 9.36 vs (6, 5) 9.38 mm); the chosen one is second in both and the only one at the top of both. The rule uses no dynamics (the second independent verification had run this odd-end I / L exchange once as a sensitivity; its result is not an input). Fixed on geometry alone before any dynamics run of the candidates (2026-11-17 09:41 UTC)
hook_roles.sensitivity: the maintainers' measurement of the hook assignments (ysim 0.3.1, not published; every one of the 64 assignments the guide allows: 11 primitives x 4 successive executions from stand in the default mode, and the 9 forward rolls from the stand face and after one roll with the authors' code (mode hardware) and with a uniform 15 % band; consequences, never used to choose): all 64 rest stably (44/44 at rest, 0 timeouts, 0 end triangles); mean heading per forward roll on the faces the robot lives on -25.7...+1.2 deg (median -11.6, quartiles -16.1...-9.5; single rolls -63.1...+31.2 deg), the 8 nearest the authors' model -15.7...-8.9 deg, the chosen -12.2 deg, 0.3.0's rule -21.3 deg; distance per roll 0.225-0.265 m, duration 7.2-9.5 s; with the default 5 % band 46 of 64 tip every roll in every execution; with the authors' 15 % band 0-18 of 18 rolls tip (median 6; the chosen 3, 0.3.0's 0; (4, 6) and (4, 7) all 18), with the authors' code verbatim some rolls tip in 16 of 64 assignments (at most 13 / 18, (4, 6)). This spread is the model's real uncertainty: there is no public record of how the real robot is strung
